findings.title: AntigravityExecutor drains stdout then stderr serially, has no cancellation, and its watchdog only kills the direct child: a GCD worker, continuation, 2 pipes and a Process can be pinned per refresh
findings.evidence: L80-103: withCheckedThrowingContinuation { DispatchQueue.global(...).async { timer.schedule(deadline: .now() + 35); timer.setEventHandler { if process.isRunning { process.terminate() } } ... let outData = stdout.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile(); let errData = stderr.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile(); process.waitUntilExit() }. (1) Serial drain: if agy writes more than the 64 KB pipe buffer to stderr before closing stdout, the child blocks on write(stderr) while we block on read(stdout). Only the 35 s SIGTERM breaks it, so each refresh parks a worker for 35 s and then fails. (2) EOF on stdout needs every holder of the write end to close it. The timer checks process.isRunning, which is false once agy exits. So if agy leaves a helper holding the inherited pipe, nothing unblocks the read: the worker thread, continuation, fds and Process are leaked. The 186 MB Go binary at ~/.local/bin/agy has daemon/setsid strings; not confirmed by running it. (3) No withTaskCancellationHandler: VendorViewModel.refresh cancels the Task, but the child and continuation keep running, and every forced or credential-watcher refresh starts another agy. Growth: up to 1 thread + 4 fds + 1 child per Gemini refresh (300 s cadence plus manual clicks); the GCD pool is capped at about 64 threads.
findings.impact: Starves DispatchQueue.global (also used by the SecurityToolCredentialReader drain) and leaks fds and child processes over long uptime. Even without the descendant case, a stderr-heavy agy turns every Gemini refresh into a 35 s timeout.
findings.fix: Drain stdout and stderr concurrently (readabilityHandler or two async reads), each capped at a byte limit (e.g. 1 MiB). Wrap the continuation in withTaskCancellationHandler so cancellation terminates the child and resumes once. On timeout, close the parent read ends and SIGKILL after SIGTERM, ideally for the whole process group.

test_red_green.name: AntigravityExecutorTests.stderrFloodDoesNotDeadlock + cancelTerminatesChild
test_red_green.assert_before: A customPath script writing 200 KB to stderr first takes >= 35 s; one that backgrounds sleep 600 holding stdout never returns; after Task.cancel the child pid is still alive
test_red_green.assert_after: Both return in < 2 s with a bounded error; after cancel, kill(pid,0) == ESRCH within 1 s; fd count unchanged after 50 iterations

findings.cetico_evidence: AntigravityExecutor.swift:80-103: the drains are sequential, and withCheckedThrowingContinuation has no withTaskCancellationHandler, so a cancel does not kill the child. The worker is still freed within 35 s via SIGTERM. The descendant-holds-pipe leak did not reproduce: the real agy's --bg-updater child did not keep the pipe, and the call exited normally.

findings.title: A cancelled transcript scan calls memo.retain(paths:) with a partial seenPaths set and evicts every entry it did not reach
findings.evidence: L65 `if Task.isCancelled { break }` leaves the walker early, then L116 `memo.retain(paths: seenPaths)` runs anyway (ScanMemo.swift:75 `entries = entries.filter { paths.contains($0.key) }`). CodexSessionScanner has the same pattern at L105 (break) and L153 (retain). CostEstimator.refresh cancels the in-flight scan on supersession (CostEstimator.swift:103).
findings.impact: Bounded (7-day window), not a leak. But the next pass re-parses cold (the file comment measures 191 MB / 839 files, 2-6 s CPU) and briefly maps large Data again, so supersession churn means repeated cold scans and RSS spikes.
findings.fix: Only prune when the walk finished: `if !Task.isCancelled { memo.retain(paths: seenPaths) }` in both scanners.

test_red_green.name: ScanMemoTests.cancelledScanKeepsUnvisitedEntries
test_red_green.assert_before: memo seeded with N files; scan cancelled after the first file -> memo.count == 1
test_red_green.assert_after: memo.count == N; a completed scan still prunes aged-out paths

findings.cetico_evidence: ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:65 breaks on cancel, and :116 memo.retain(paths: seenPaths) still runs with the partial set. CodexSessionScanner.swift:105/:153 does the same. CostEstimator.swift:103 cancels scans when a new one supersedes them. The result is a cold rescan (CPU) and no leak.

findings.title: AnalyticsStore.recompute decodes the full 90-day history JSONL for every vendor, synchronously on main, twice per cost refresh
findings.evidence: L202-204 historyProvider = { vendor in (try? UsageHistoryStore.defaultFor(vendor))?.load(since: Date().addingTimeInterval(-90 * 86_400)) ?? [] }. L256 calls it for every vendor in recompute(). The costEstimator.$byVendor sink (~L209) fires twice per scan because CostEstimator.swift:138-139 assigns byVendor[.anthropic] and byVendor[.openai] separately. That is about 25.9k samples per vendor at 300 s cadence.
findings.impact: Not retained, but it causes periodic MB-scale allocation bursts and main-thread stalls that grow linearly with history size up to the 90-day retention cap.
findings.fix: Cache samples per vendor and append incrementally (VendorViewModel already has the live tail), or load in Task.detached. Coalesce the two byVendor writes.

test_red_green.name: AnalyticsStoreTests.recomputeDoesNotReloadHistoryPerEmission
test_red_green.assert_before: counting historyProvider called 2 x vendors times per CostEstimator publish

findings.cetico_evidence: Same root cause as PERF-FLU-001 (AnalyticsStore.swift:202-204, 255-256; CostEstimator.swift:138-139). The allocations are transient and not retained. Fold it into PERF-FLU-001.

findings.title: Downloaded DMG temp file is not deleted when the status, size or checksum check fails
findings.evidence: L248 `let (tmp, http) = try await self.http.download(req)`, then throws at L250 (non-2xx), L256 (size mismatch) and L262 (checksum mismatch). Only the success path at L265 moves tmp. The async URLSession.download(for:) does not delete the returned file. HTTPClient.download (HTTPClient.swift:71-76) also drops tmp on its post-download throws.
findings.impact: Each failed update attempt leaves a DMG-sized file in the temp dir. User-triggered, so growth is per click.
findings.fix: `defer { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: tmp) }` after download (a no-op once moved), plus cleanup in the HTTPClient.download throw paths.
findings.cetico_evidence: UpdateChecker.swift:248-263: the throws for non-2xx, size mismatch and checksum mismatch all leave the URLSession download tmp in place, and only the success path moves it (L265). HTTPClient.swift:73-75 drops tmp on its non-HTTP throw too. It is user-triggered and $TMPDIR is purged by the OS eventually, hence LOW.

findings.title: Re-login spawns an untracked zsh -l -c <login> per click with no handle, termination or single-flight
findings.evidence: `let task = Process(); task.launchPath = "/bin/zsh"; task.arguments = ["-l", "-c", command]; try task.run()`. The Process is a local and is never stored, waited on or terminated. reloginPending re-arms after 120 s (L538-541). An abandoned OAuth login CLI waits for its browser callback indefinitely, so each retry adds another long-lived process tree with its own callback listener.
findings.impact: Grows by one process tree per abandoned retry, bounded by clicks. Duplicate listeners can also make later logins fail.
findings.fix: Keep the Process on VendorViewModel; do not re-spawn while it isRunning (or terminate the old one first); terminate it when needsReauth flips false.

test_red_green.name: ReloginSpawnerTests.secondClickDoesNotStackProcesses
test_red_green.assert_before: two spawns of sleep 600 -> 2 live pids
test_red_green.assert_after: 1 live pid; the old pid is ESRCH

findings.cetico_evidence: VendorSectionView.swift:524-528 keeps the Process in a local variable and never tracks or stops it. The button is disabled for 120 s (:503, :533), so the growth is at most one tree per 120 s of user clicks. The claim that an abandoned claude/codex login waits for its callback forever was not verified.

findings.title: HTTPClient.send buffers whole responses with no size cap (vendor usage, OAuth refresh, GitHub release and checksum fetches)
findings.evidence: `let (data, response) = try await session.data(for: req)` has no limit. sendBounded (L132-187) exists but only the status sources use it. sendDecoding (OpenRouter, xAI), OAuthRefresher.swift:28 and UpdateChecker.swift:159/294 use the unbounded send, and CachedFetch persists the body to DiskCache.
findings.impact: Transient, not retained: an oversized body from an allowlisted or compromised endpoint forces an arbitrarily large allocation per 300 s refresh and the same bytes are written to the disk cache.
findings.fix: Route provider, OAuth and update JSON through sendBounded (2-4 MiB), or give send() a default cap.
findings.cetico_evidence: Duplicate of BP-REP-001, same site: HTTPClient.swift:108. The same downgrade reasoning applies.

findings.title: NotificationService.highestNotified keeps an orphan key every month for the xAI Monthly (YYYY-MM) window label
findings.evidence: The key is vendor:window.label, and XAIWireTypes.swift:362/381/388 builds the label as Monthly (%04d-%02d). A key is removed only when that same key drops below the minimum threshold (L75-76), so a key from a past cycle that crossed a threshold is never removed.
findings.impact: +1 tiny entry per month, negligible. The path is also disabled on macOS 26.
findings.fix: Prune the keys of this vendor that are absent from snapshot.windows at the end of observe().
findings.cetico_evidence: NotificationService.swift:70-76 only removes a key when the same label drops below the threshold, so a monthly label leaves one tiny orphan entry each month. The whole path is off on macOS 26 (:65 isRuntimeKnownIncompatible).

findings.title: RefreshScheduler loops upgrade [weak self] to strong for the whole infinite loop, so the cancels in deinit can never run
findings.evidence: `refreshLoop = Task { @MainActor [weak self] in guard let self else { return } ... while !Task.isCancelled { ... } }`. The same pattern is at L62 and L148, giving self -> Task -> self. compactLoop (L128) correctly uses self? per iteration.
findings.impact: No growth today: a single scheduler is created in App.init (AiTaskbarApp.swift:67). It would leak, with duplicate refresh fan-out, if a scheduler is ever rebuilt without calling stop().
findings.fix: Re-bind weakly per iteration, as compactLoop does.

test_red_green.name: RefreshSchedulerTests.deinitCancelsLoops
test_red_green.assert_before: weak ref still non-nil after the last strong ref is dropped
test_red_green.assert_after: weak ref is nil and the refreshAll counter stops

findings.cetico_evidence: RefreshScheduler.swift:62/77 turn the weak self into a strong reference for the whole loop. There is a single scheduler for the app's lifetime and stop() exists, so there is no growth.
